## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports). `orderByClause` stays an allowlisted switch.

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`. Hierarchy permission policy lives in the service, but the HTTP layer never supplies the authenticated subject, so promote/demote/set-manager authorize a body id. The same service returns payroll fields from an unauthenticated read and can `ALTER TABLE` on that path. Comment ownership compares the stored author to a client field.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controllers.** Notifications `validateOwnership` compares `:userId` to `req.user.userId` (94–110). Community-challenge PUT/DELETE require the creator (908–1072) while get and join ignore `is_public`. Post DELETE uses `getSessionUserId`; comment PUT/DELETE use the client id. `setManager` checks admin only when a requester id is supplied. `promoteToAdmin` checks the body id's roles and then fails open on the pull. `GET hierarchy/tree` has no actor at all. `AdminAuthGuard` is role-based (249–253) and therefore trusts whatever roles `resolve-id` copied after that write. `SessionController` is registered in every environment. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`.

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on stats, entries, PUT, and DELETE; personal challenges scope timer reads to `CurrentUser()`; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2 once the shared limiter allows the call; CRM PATCH uses hardcoded column names; community-challenge `ORDER BY` uses an allowlist plus `pg-format` `%I`; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/`; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`; dedicated-item and personal-challenge updates go through class-validator DTOs. Collection names are checked against `ALLOWED_COLLECTIONS` before SQL.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox, and promote-admin can add that role for any directory admin id. NFR §3.5 data minimization is missed by the public hierarchy tree.

**Delta vs 2026-09-26:** No product commits (`HEAD` still `3d92f9d`). Previously confirmed critical items re-verified at the same line numbers. **New first-class critical:** a public admin id is enough to grant `admin`. `GET /api/users` and `GET /api/users/search` have no guard and return `id`, `email`, and `roles` (`user-profile.service.ts` 68–75, 503–516). `POST /api/users/:id/promote-admin` is `JwtAuthGuard` only and does not pass `req.user` (`users.controller.ts` 64–70). `promoteToAdmin` loads roles for body `requestingAdminId` and, when that row is an admin, writes `roles` including `admin` and sets `parent_manager_id` to that id (`user-hierarchy.service.ts` 945–1049). `assertRequesterMayPullTargetUnderSelf` returns success unless the named admin is already above the target or the target is an ancestor of that admin (93–149). Unguarded controllers unchanged: community-members, crm, items-delivery, places, rate-limit, redis-test, rides, dedicated-items, collections, session (health excluded). `ThrottlerModule` still has no `APP_GUARD`. No `trust proxy` under `apps/api`. ## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Public admin UUID grants the `admin` role (2026-09-27).** `POST /api/users/:id/promote-admin` requires only `JwtAuthGuard`. The handler forwards `{ requestingAdminId }` and never reads `req.user` (`users.controller.ts` 64–70). `promoteToAdmin` requires that body id, loads that row, and continues when its `roles` include `admin` or `super_admin` (`user-hierarchy.service.ts` 945–981, 1035–1049). The hierarchy helper fails open: it returns success when the named admin is not already above the target and the target is not an ancestor (93–149). `GET /api/users` (no guard) selects `id`, `email`, and `roles` (`user-profile.service.ts` 503–516); search does the same (68–75). Register inserts no `parent_manager_id` (`user-auth.service.ts` 101–112), so a new account is eligible. Concrete trigger: read an admin id from `GET /api/users`, obtain any access token (including `POST /api/users/resolve-id` with a known email), then `POST /api/users/<targetId>/promote-admin` with that admin id. A second `resolve-id` mints a JWT whose `roles` come from the database (645–660) and passes `AdminAuthGuard` (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 238–264). The root-admin mailbox is still rejected as the promote target (993–1002). `POST :id/promote-volunteer` is the same actor spoof and adds `volunteer` (82–88, 1306–1407). `POST :id/demote-admin` applies the named admin's authority to that admin's subtree, and a public `super_admin` id skips the subordinate check (75–80, 1120–1194). This is distinct from the 2026-09-25 set-manager omit path, which does not add `admin`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (40–43, 64–88, 135–150, 183–188); `apps/api/src/services/user-hierarchy.service.ts` (93–149, 945–1068, 1120–1194, 1306–1407); `apps/api/src/services/user-profile.service.ts` (68–75, 503–516); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (101–112, 645–660) -> Action: Bind the actor to `req.user.userId` and require `AdminAuthGuard` on promote, demote, and promote-volunteer. Fail closed in `assertRequesterMayPullTargetUnderSelf`. Stop returning `roles` from unauthenticated directory and search. Stop minting tokens from `resolve-id`.

 * **Comment edit/delete IDOR: ownership is the client `user_id`, not the JWT subject (2026-09-26, re-verified 2026-09-27).** `PUT` and `DELETE /api/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId` use `JwtAuthGuard` and then ignore `req.user`. Update allows the write when `body.user_id` equals `post_comments.user_id` (`posts.controller.ts` 1975–2024). Delete uses query `user_id` (2053–2106) and rewrites `posts.comments`. Unguarded `GET :postId/comments` returns `c.user_id` (1726–1743). Any access token, including one from `resolve-id`, can edit or delete. Post PUT/hide/unhide still prefer `req.user.userId`; post DELETE uses `getSessionUserId` with no body fallback. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (1726–1743, 1975–2142) -> Action: Bind the actor to `req.user.userId`. Reject a mismatched body or query `user_id`. Do not return raw `error.message` from the catch blocks.

 * **Unauthenticated org-tree rewrite via email-only `resolve-id` and omitted `requestingUserId` (2026-09-25, re-verified 2026-09-27).** `POST /api/users/resolve-id` mints a JWT from email, `google_id`, or `firebase_uid` (`user-auth.service.ts` 270–342, 645–660). `POST /api/users/:id/set-manager` never reads `req.user` (`users.controller.ts` 45–52). Omitting `requestingUserId`, or sending an unknown id, skips the admin check (`user-hierarchy.service.ts` 492–516) and writes `parent_manager_id` (600–628). `POST :id/hierarchy/manage` has no actor field (55–62, 871–914). The root-admin email cannot be the set-manager target. The 2026-09-27 bullet is the separate case where a real, public admin id is supplied to promote-admin. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (45–62, 183–188); `apps/api/src/services/user-hierarchy.service.ts` (492–516, 600–628, 871–914); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (270–342, 645–660) -> Action: Bind the actor to `req.user.userId` and require `AdminAuthGuard`.  * **Unauthenticated one-request lockout of password-verified `/session/login` (2026-09-24, re-verified 2026-09-27).** `RateLimitController` has no `UseGuards`. `POST /rate-limit/stress-test` loops `checkRateLimit` up to 50 times and defaults `identifier` to `@Ip()` (`rate-limit.controller.ts` 59–84). Count login failures per account after a password check. Do not let anonymous callers choose `ruleType` or `identifier`.

 * **Unauthenticated one-shot plant of the shared JOSE JWT lockout (2026-09-23, re-verified 2026-09-27).** `POST /rate-limit/custom` forwards `identifier`, `rule`, and `customKey` into `applyCustomRateLimit` (`rate-limit.service.ts` 269–275). Blocks are stored at `blocked:<ruleType>:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `JwtAuthGuard` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` under `api_access` before `verifyToken` (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–114). The body type is a TypeScript interface, so `ValidationPipe` does not whitelist it. `requests: 0` with a positive `blockDurationMs` and `customKey` `api_access` writes the shared HS256 block on the first call. `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can remove it. NFR §3.1 currently requires “per token prefix”; that sentence is the defect. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (20–21, 151–168, 233–248); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141, 269–275); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134) -> Action: Remove `RateLimitController` from deployed builds or require admin JWT. Ignore client `customKey` and cap `blockDurationMs`. Change §3.1 so the limit is per verified caller after `verifyToken`.

 * **Shared JOSE-header rate-limit lockout on every JWT route (2026-09-22, re-verified 2026-09-27).** Independent of the plant above, one hundred requests with a forged Bearer that uses the standard HS256 header write the same block key for 300 seconds (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–115). ## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Hierarchy pull check fails open (2026-09-27).** `assertRequesterMayPullTargetUnderSelf` returns `{ ok: true }` when neither “admin is above target” nor “target is an ancestor of the admin” is true (`user-hierarchy.service.ts` 149). A profile with `parent_manager_id` null therefore always passes. Recommendation: Default to deny. Allow the pull only when the authenticated admin is already the manager, or when an explicit super-admin rule says so.

 * **Comment handlers return `error.message` to the client (re-verified 2026-09-27).** Update, delete, and list catch blocks interpolate the driver message into the JSON body (`posts.controller.ts` 2042–2045, 2134–2137, 1803–1805). `getUserById`, sync, and admin-tables do the same. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log the driver message server-side.

 * **`GET /rate-limit/stats` lists every limiter key with no auth (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `getRateLimitStats` runs `KEYS rate_limit:*` and `KEYS blocked:*` (`rate-limit.service.ts` 238–256; controller 213–221). `GET /rate-limit/status` answers the same question for a chosen identifier. Recommendation: Remove both routes from deployed builds.

 * **Rate limiter fails open when Redis errors (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `checkRateLimit` returns `allowed: true` if the block read or the counter read throws (`rate-limit.service.ts` 87–89, 106–111). Recommendation: Fail closed on auth routes when the limiter cannot be read.

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics (re-verified 2026-09-27).** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` and clears stats caches (373–401). `POST /api/stats/increment` uses `AdminAuthGuard`. Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token, or drop the public increment.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s posts and follows (776–782). Recommendation: Require JWT and bind the viewer to `req.user.userId`.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` and only then flips the ride to `full`. It does not reject when approved seats would exceed `available_seats`. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `popular-collections` and `cache-stats`. Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized routes.

 * **`loginUser` and `JwtAuthGuard` never consult `user_profiles.is_active` (re-verified 2026-09-27).** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified and not implemented (re-verified 2026-09-27).** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent (0 matches under `apps/`). Recommendation: Add the column and the feed projection. Do not treat that as a drive-by security hotfix.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log and record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `userId` from the JWT and then insert any `challengeId`. Recommendation: Insert only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (re-verified 2026-09-27).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws (123–125) and the inner catch tries Firebase (126–133). An HS256 refresh token does not verify as a Firebase ID token. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. Verification always uses HMAC-SHA256, so `none` / RS256 confusion does not apply to this verifier. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL (75). Autocomplete encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup and register enumeration (re-verified 2026-09-27).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `email OR firebase_uid OR google_id` using body `firebaseUid` (723–746). `POST /auth/register` returns `Email already registered` (415–418). Recommendation: Match only the verified Google `sub` or verified email. Return a generic register result.

 * **Web refresh tokens sit in AsyncStorage (re-verified 2026-09-27).** `tokenManager.web.ts` writes `auth_access_token` and `auth_refresh_token` through AsyncStorage, which is `localStorage` on web. Recommendation: Keep the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie on web.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports). `orderByClause` stays an allowlisted switch.

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`. Hierarchy permission policy lives in the service, but the HTTP layer never supplies the authenticated subject, so promote/demote/set-manager authorize a body id. Comment ownership compares the stored author to a client field.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controllers.** Notifications `validateOwnership` compares `:userId` to `req.user.userId` (94–110). Community-challenge PUT/DELETE require the creator (908–1072) while get and join ignore `is_public`. Post DELETE uses `getSessionUserId`; comment PUT/DELETE use the client id. `setManager` checks admin only when a requester id is supplied. `promoteToAdmin` checks the body id's roles and then fails open on the pull. `AdminAuthGuard` is role-based (249–253) and therefore trusts whatever roles `resolve-id` copied after that write. `SessionController` is registered in every environment. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`.

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on stats, entries, PUT, and DELETE; personal challenges scope timer reads to `CurrentUser()`; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2 once the shared limiter allows the call; CRM PATCH uses hardcoded column names; community-challenge `ORDER BY` uses an allowlist plus `pg-format` `%I`; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/`; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`; dedicated-item and personal-challenge updates go through class-validator DTOs. Collection names are checked against `ALLOWED_COLLECTIONS` before SQL.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox, and promote-admin can now add that role for any directory admin id.

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Comment edit/delete IDOR: ownership is the client `user_id`, not the JWT subject (2026-09-26).** `PUT /api/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId` and `DELETE /api/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId` use `JwtAuthGuard` and then ignore `req.user`. Update requires `body.user_id` and proceeds when it equals `post_comments.user_id` (`posts.controller.ts` 1985–2024). Delete requires query `user_id` and does the same (2058–2092), then sets `posts.comments` from a fresh count (2095–2106). `GET :postId/comments` is unauthenticated and selects `c.user_id` (1726–1743). The 2026-09-13 bullet covers creating likes and comments as another user; this path rewrites or removes an existing comment. Any access token is enough, and `POST /api/users/resolve-id` still mints one from a known email. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (1726–1743, 1975–2142) -> Action: Bind the actor to `req.user.userId`. Reject a body or query `user_id` that does not match. Do not return raw `error.message` from the catch blocks (2003–2045, 2121–2137).

 * **Unauthenticated org-tree rewrite via email-only `resolve-id` and omitted `requestingUserId` (2026-09-25, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `POST /api/users/resolve-id` looks up `user_profiles` by email, `google_id`, or `firebase_uid` and returns a JWT pair (`user-auth.service.ts` 270–342, 645–660). `POST /api/users/:id/set-manager` is `JwtAuthGuard` only. The controller passes the body through and does not pass `req.user` (`users.controller.ts` 45–52). `setManagerEnsureRequesterAdminIfProvided` allows the call when `requestingUserId` is missing or unknown (492–516). The service then sets `parent_manager_id` (600–628). `POST :id/hierarchy/manage` likewise ignores the JWT subject and applies `action: add|remove` for the body `managerId` (55–62, 871–914). `GET /api/users` is unauthenticated, so target ids are public. The root-admin email cannot be the set-manager target. `promoteToAdmin` still requires a real admin id in the body; the omit bypass is specific to `setManager`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (45–62, 183–188); `apps/api/src/services/user-hierarchy.service.ts` (492–516, 600–628, 871–914); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (270–342, 645–660) -> Action: Bind the actor to `req.user.userId` and require `AdminAuthGuard`. Fail closed when the requester is missing. Stop minting tokens from `resolve-id`.

 * **Unauthenticated one-request lockout of password-verified `/session/login` (2026-09-24, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `RateLimitController` has no `UseGuards`. `POST /rate-limit/stress-test` loops `checkRateLimit(identifier, ruleType)` up to 50 times and defaults `identifier` to `@Ip()` (`rate-limit.controller.ts` 59–84). The built-in `login` rule allows 5 requests per 15 minutes and then sets `blockDurationMs` to 30 minutes (`rate-limit.service.ts` 36–40). The sixth call writes `blocked:login:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `POST /session/login` reads that key with the same `@Ip()` before `argon2.verify` (`session.controller.ts` 42–65, 96) and returns "Too many login attempts". No `trust proxy` setting exists under `apps/api`, so `@Ip()` is the immediate TCP peer. Behind the committed Railway proxy, every client of that process shares the peer, and one stress-test locks session login for all of them. The response body includes the identifier. `POST /rate-limit/test` and `POST /rate-limit/simulate/login` write the same key one call at a time (28–54, 270–287). `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can delete it. `SessionController` is registered in every environment (`app.module.ts` 97). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (28–117, 151–168, 233–287); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (36–40, 82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (42–130); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (97) -> Action: Do not mount `RateLimitController` on deployed builds. Count login failures per account after a password check, not per raw peer address. Set `trust proxy` only for a proxy you trust, and still do not let anonymous callers choose `ruleType` or `identifier`.

 * **Unauthenticated one-shot plant of the shared JOSE JWT lockout (2026-09-23, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `POST /rate-limit/custom` forwards `body.identifier`, `body.rule`, and `body.customKey` into `applyCustomRateLimit`, which sets the Redis rule type to `customKey` (`rate-limit.service.ts` 269–275). `checkRateLimit` stores blocks at `blocked:<ruleType>:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `JwtAuthGuard` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` under rule type `api_access` before signature verification (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 97–114). Compact HS256 headers share one 16-character prefix. Concrete trigger: `POST /rate-limit/custom` with that prefix as `identifier`, `customKey` `api_access`, and `rule.requests` `0` plus a positive `blockDurationMs`, and no `Authorization`. `requests: 0` makes the first call a block. Every later HS256 access token then receives `UnauthorizedException("Rate limit exceeded")`. `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can delete that block with no auth. NFR §3.1 currently requires “per token prefix”; that sentence is the defect (SRS §10.3). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (20–21, 151–168, 233–248); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141, 181–191, 269–275); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (276–291) -> Action: Remove `RateLimitController` from deployed builds or require admin JWT; ignore client `customKey` and cap `blockDurationMs`; change §3.1 so the limit is per verified caller after `verifyToken`; keep forged-token abuse on a separate IP bucket.

 * **Shared JOSE-header rate-limit lockout on every JWT route (2026-09-22, re-verified 2026-09-26).** Independent of the plant above, `JwtAuthGuard.canActivate` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` before `verifyToken` and throws when the shared bucket is blocked (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–115). One hundred requests with a forged Bearer that uses the standard HS256 header write the same block key for 300 seconds. Ordinary traffic does the same once the whole user base exceeds 100 authenticated calls in one minute. RS256 Firebase tokens share a second global bucket. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (278); `docs/SSOT/SRS/03-non-functional-requirements.md` (§3.1) -> Action: Same as the plant bullet: key on the verified user id after `verifyToken`.

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` returns refresh-token keys (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: list those keys, fetch one, then `POST /auth/refresh` mints an access token that copies `payload.roles`. `POST /redis-test/set` and `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` overwrite or delete refresh, blacklist, and cache keys. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` on any deployed environment; never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the Redis instance that stores refresh tokens.

 * **Unauthenticated guest read-receipt forge / unread wipe (2026-09-16, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `OptionalAuthGuard` always returns true (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 338). `POST /api/chat/conversations/:conversationId/read-all` sets `authenticatedUserId = req.user?.userId || body?.user_id` (679). With no JWT, a body user id that is a participant inserts `message_read_receipts` for every unread message. `POST /api/chat/messages/:messageId/read` uses the same fallback (759). Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization` → `POST /api/chat/conversations/<id>/read-all` `{ "user_id": "<victim>" }`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (45–46, 671–743, 751–812); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (308–338) -> Action: Require JWT on mark-read; bind the reader to `req.user.userId`; delete the body `user_id` fallback.

Guest `GET /conversations/<id>/messages` (378–387) selects by id with no participant check. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (246–330, 378–387) -> Action: Require JWT; bind `:userId` to `req.user.userId`; delete the guest branch.

Guest send skips participant membership and can auto-create a thread. Guest create returns `SELECT *` of an existing participant set. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (107–230, 441–569) -> Action: Require JWT; require the sender to be a participant; do not return an existing DM to a guest.

 * **Unauthenticated ride POST/PUT/DELETE + driver PII dump (2026-09-05, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `RidesController` has no `UseGuards`. GET returns `driver_phone` / email. Writes are unauthenticated and can insert legacy `user_profiles`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rides.controller.ts` -> Action: Add `JwtAuthGuard`; bind the owner to the JWT; strip driver PII from public list/detail.

 * **Donation actor spoof + unauthenticated dumps + JWT PUT/DELETE IDOR.** JWT `POST /api/donations` inserts body `donor_id`. `PUT :id` / `DELETE :id` are `JwtAuthGuard` only. `GET /` selects `d.*`. `GET :id` returns donor phone/email. Knowledge-link `POST /api/donations/knowledge/links` is public and accepts spoofable `createdByUserId`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/donations.controller.ts` -> Action: Bind `donor_id` to the JWT; require ownership or admin on PUT/DELETE; auth-gate list and detail; require JWT on knowledge-link create.

 * **JWT-gated task actor spoof + unscoped reads.** `POST /api/tasks/:id/log-hours` upserts as body `user_id`. `GET /api/tasks` is unscoped. `GET :id`, subtasks, and tree embed emails. `GET hours-report/:managerId` has no owner/admin check. - File: `apps/api/src/tasks/tasks.controller.ts` -> Action: Bind actors to `req.user.userId`; scope reads to owner, assignee, or admin.

 * **Fully unguarded write surfaces (items-delivery, dedicated-items, collections, CRM, community-members, rate-limit, places).** No `UseGuards`. Items-delivery trusts body `owner_id`. Dedicated-items and collections (`userId=all`) are unauthenticated CRUD over JSONB including chats, messages, and notifications. CRM selects all rows. Community-members returns `contact_info`. Rate-limit `DELETE /clear`, `POST /custom`, `POST /test`, and `POST /stress-test` can wipe or plant blocks. `GET /rate-limit/stats` lists every rate-limit and block key. Places proxies `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/items-delivery.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/items/dedicated-items.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/items/items.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/controllers/crm.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/controllers/community-members.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/controllers/places.controller.ts` -> Action: Add `JwtAuthGuard` (admin where appropriate); bind owners to the JWT; do not expose rate-limit mutation or the places proxy on deployed environments.

 * **JWT-only stats email export (re-verified 2026-09-26).** `GET /api/stats/analytics/users` uses `AdminAuthGuard` (499). `GET /api/stats/details/:statType` uses `JwtAuthGuard` only (834–835). `totalUsers` selects `name`, `email`, and `city` for up to 500 rows (862–876). The cache key is global. `GET /api/stats/analytics/categories` and `GET /api/stats/real-time` have no guard (439, 782). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/stats.controller.ts` (439–463, 782–810, 834–876) -> Action: Put `details/:statType` behind `AdminAuthGuard`; drop email from the default export.

 * **Admin-files list ACL too weak.** `GET /api/admin-files` and `GET folders` are `JwtAuthGuard` only. POST/DELETE use `AdminAuthGuard`. Any authenticated user can list Finance/HR file URLs. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/admin-files.controller.ts` (80–203) -> Action: Put list and folders behind `AdminAuthGuard`.

 * **Community daily-tracker IDOR.** The class is JWT-gated, but `GET daily-tracker` uses query `user_id` (288–336), not `req.user`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (288–336) -> Action: Bind `user_id` to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **Request-path `DROP TABLE ... CASCADE`.** `ensurePostsTable` (used from post routes) drops `posts` when legacy columns are detected (78), plus likes/comments (309, 373–374). `tasks-schema.service.ts` (41) can drop `posts`. `DatabaseInit` drops donations/rides on startup (568, 670) when it treats the schema as legacy. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (78, 309, 373–374); `apps/api/src/tasks/tasks-schema.service.ts` (41); `apps/api/src/database/database.init.ts` (568, 670) -> Action: Never DROP on a request path; gate destructive DDL behind an explicit offline migration.

 * **Committed credentials, backups, and env fingerprints.** `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` line 34 commits a `JWT_SECRET` (value not repeated here). `docs/SSOT/runbooks/api/environment-separation.md` line 126 documents a real-looking JWT value (not repeated here). `main.ts` 149–218 fingerprints environments with committed DB/Redis password and host substrings (values not repeated here). 49 tracked JSON files under `apps/api/data-backups/20251224-162421/` include `user_profiles` email, phone, and `password_hash`. - File: `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (34); `apps/api/src/main.ts` (149–218); `apps/api/data-backups/` -> Action: Rotate every fingerprinted credential; replace substring detection with an explicit `ENVIRONMENT` flag; purge backups from git history; store JWT secrets outside the repo.

Combined with the redis-test harvest, elevated roles survive demotion for the refresh TTL (30 days). SRS §2.1.4 expects a reload. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (146–177) -> Action: Reload roles from the database on refresh; rotate refresh tokens.

 * **Google `/auth/google` access-token fallback.** If `idToken` verification fails, the handler fetches Google userinfo with a client-supplied `accessToken` and provisions a login with `emailVerified: true` hardcoded. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/auth.controller.ts` (588–698) -> Action: Accept only verified Google/Firebase ID tokens.

## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Comment handlers return `error.message` to the client (2026-09-26).** The new IDOR's catch blocks return `Failed to update comment: ${errorMessage}` and the delete/list equivalents (`posts.controller.ts` 2042–2045, 2134–2137, 1803–1805). A database error becomes part of the JSON body. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log the driver message server-side.

 * **`GET /rate-limit/stats` lists every limiter key with no auth (2026-09-24, re-verified 2026-09-26).** `getRateLimitStats` runs `KEYS rate_limit:*` and `KEYS blocked:*` and returns the key strings (`rate-limit.service.ts` 238–256; controller 213–221). Identifiers embedded in those keys (peer addresses, JOSE prefixes, whatever `/custom` stored) are readable by anyone. `GET /rate-limit/status` answers the same question for a chosen identifier and rule type (124–141). Recommendation: Remove both routes from deployed builds.

 * **Rate limiter fails open when Redis errors.** `checkRateLimit` returns `allowed: true` if the block read or the counter read throws (`rate-limit.service.ts` 87–89, 106–111). A Redis blip disables both the JOSE bucket and the login block. Recommendation: Fail closed on auth routes when the limiter cannot be read.

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics.** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` for `CURRENT_DATE` and clears stats caches (373–401). `POST /api/stats/increment` uses `AdminAuthGuard`. Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token, or drop the public increment.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s posts and follows (776–782) and drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT and bind the viewer to `req.user.userId`.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` and only then flips the ride to `full`. It does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `popular-collections` and `cache-stats`. Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized routes.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified and not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent (0 matches under `apps/`). Public feed returns author `id`, `name`, and `avatar_url`. Recommendation: Add the column and the feed projection; do not treat that as a drive-by security hotfix.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log / record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `userId` from the JWT and then insert any `challengeId`. `GET reset-logs/all` and `GET record-breaks/all` are scoped to `CurrentUser()` (548–571, 629–652). Recommendation: Insert only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws (123–125), and the inner `catch` tries Firebase (126–133). An HS256 refresh token does not verify as a Firebase ID token. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; fall back to Firebase only when signature verification fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. The header `alg` is not read; verification always uses HMAC-SHA256, so `none` / RS256 confusion does not apply to this verifier. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check, and still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** The catch returns `details: error?.message`. Sync user/all and admin-tables handlers do the same. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log details server-side.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL (75). Autocomplete encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register / resolve-id).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `email OR firebase_uid OR google_id` using body `firebaseUid` (723–746), updates identity columns (773–784), and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only the verified Google `sub` or verified email.

 * **`POST /auth/register` returns `Email already registered` (415–418)** despite an anti-enumeration comment. `GET /auth/check-email` already exposes existence by design. Recommendation: Return a generic result and throttle the check.

 * **Web refresh tokens sit in AsyncStorage.** `tokenManager.web.ts` writes `auth_access_token` and `auth_refresh_token` through AsyncStorage, which is `localStorage` on web. Recommendation: Keep the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie on web; leave native SecureStore as it is.

 * **ClosedRoute still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and `user?: any`.** File: `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx`. Recommendation: Use the shared logger and drop the inline `require`.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports). `orderByClause` stays an allowlisted switch.

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`. Hierarchy permission policy lives in the service, but the HTTP layer never supplies the authenticated subject, so the policy cannot see the caller. Comment ownership is implemented in the controller and compares the stored author to a client field instead of the session.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controller.** Chat binds JWT conversation lists to self and still dumps any inbox for guests; mark-read falls back to body `user_id`. Community challenges bind PUT/DELETE to the creator and still ignore `is_public` on list, get, and join. Posts hide hidden status on the public feed only. Like and comment creates persist `body.user_id`. Comment PUT/DELETE check “ownership” against that same client id. Post DELETE uses `getSessionUserId` with no body fallback. Stats admin-gates `analytics/users` and `increment` and leaves `details/:statType` on `JwtAuthGuard` and `track-visit` public. `setManager` checks admin only when a requester id is supplied; `manageHierarchy` does not check admin at all. `SessionController` is registered in every environment, and its login limiter is the same Redis map an anonymous stress-test writes. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so the committed dev Railway template ships Redis `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL`. `JwtAuthGuard` applies one rate-limit bucket to every HS256 caller, and the unguarded rate-limit controller can write that same bucket. Notifications remain the in-folder contrast: `validateOwnership` compares `:userId` to `req.user.userId` (94–110).

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; personal challenges scope timers and reset-log reads to `CurrentUser()`; `NotificationsController.validateOwnership` gates mark-read and delete; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds the session user; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2 once the shared limiter allows the call; CRM PATCH interpolates hardcoded column names; community-challenge `ORDER BY` uses an allowlist plus `pg-format` `%I`; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/`; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`; dedicated-item and personal-challenge updates go through class-validator DTOs, so extra JSON keys do not become SQL identifiers. Collections names are checked against `ALLOWED_COLLECTIONS` before SQL.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox.

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Unauthenticated org-tree rewrite via email-only `resolve-id` and omitted `requestingUserId` (2026-09-25).** `POST /api/users/resolve-id` looks up `user_profiles` by email, `google_id`, or `firebase_uid` and returns a JWT pair (`user-auth.service.ts` 270–342, 645–660). `POST /api/users/:id/set-manager` is `JwtAuthGuard` only. The controller passes the body through and does not pass `req.user` (`users.controller.ts` 45–52). `setManagerEnsureRequesterAdminIfProvided` allows the call when `requestingUserId` is missing or unknown (492–516). The service then sets `parent_manager_id` (600–628). `POST :id/hierarchy/manage` likewise ignores the JWT subject and applies `action: add|remove` for the body `managerId` (55–62, 871–914). `GET /api/users` is unauthenticated, so target ids are public. The root-admin email cannot be the set-manager target. `promoteToAdmin` still requires a real admin id in the body; the omit bypass is specific to `setManager`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (45–62, 183–188); `apps/api/src/services/user-hierarchy.service.ts` (492–516, 600–628, 871–914); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (270–342, 645–660) -> Action: Bind the actor to `req.user.userId` and require `AdminAuthGuard`. Fail closed when the requester is missing. Stop minting tokens from `resolve-id`.

 * **Unauthenticated one-request lockout of password-verified `/session/login` (2026-09-24, re-verified 2026-09-25).** `RateLimitController` has no `UseGuards`. `POST /rate-limit/stress-test` loops `checkRateLimit(identifier, ruleType)` up to 50 times and defaults `identifier` to `@Ip()` (`rate-limit.controller.ts` 59–84). The built-in `login` rule allows 5 requests per 15 minutes and then sets `blockDurationMs` to 30 minutes (`rate-limit.service.ts` 36–40). The sixth call writes `blocked:login:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `POST /session/login` reads that key with the same `@Ip()` before `argon2.verify` (`session.controller.ts` 42–65, 96) and returns "Too many login attempts". No `trust proxy` setting exists under `apps/api`, so `@Ip()` is the immediate TCP peer. Behind the committed Railway proxy, every client of that process shares the peer, and one stress-test locks session login for all of them. The response body includes the identifier. `POST /rate-limit/test` and `POST /rate-limit/simulate/login` write the same key one call at a time (28–54, 270–287). `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can delete it. `SessionController` is registered in every environment (`app.module.ts` 97). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (28–117, 151–168, 233–287); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (36–40, 82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (42–130); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (97) -> Action: Do not mount `RateLimitController` on deployed builds. Count login failures per account after a password check, not per raw peer address. Set `trust proxy` only for a proxy you trust, and still do not let anonymous callers choose `ruleType` or `identifier`.

 * **Unauthenticated one-shot plant of the shared JOSE JWT lockout (2026-09-23, re-verified 2026-09-25).** `POST /rate-limit/custom` forwards `body.identifier`, `body.rule`, and `body.customKey` into `applyCustomRateLimit`, which sets the Redis rule type to `customKey` (`rate-limit.service.ts` 269–275). `checkRateLimit` stores blocks at `blocked:<ruleType>:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `JwtAuthGuard` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` under rule type `api_access` before signature verification (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 97–114). Compact HS256 headers from `jwt.service.ts` (278) start with `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1`. Concrete trigger: `POST /rate-limit/custom` with `{ "identifier": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1", "customKey": "api_access", "rule": { "requests": 0, "windowMs": 60000, "blockDurationMs": 86400000 } }` and no `Authorization`. `requests: 0` makes `validRequests.length >= rule.requests` true on the first call. Every later HS256 access token then receives `UnauthorizedException("Rate limit exceeded")`. `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can delete that block with no auth. NFR §3.1 currently requires “per token prefix”; that sentence is the defect (SRS §10.3). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (20–21, 151–168, 233–248); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141, 181–191, 269–275); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (276–291) -> Action: Remove `RateLimitController` from deployed builds or require admin JWT; ignore client `customKey` and cap `blockDurationMs`; change §3.1 so the limit is per verified caller after `verifyToken`; keep forged-token abuse on a separate IP bucket.

 * **Shared JOSE-header rate-limit lockout on every JWT route (2026-09-22, re-verified 2026-09-25).** Independent of the plant above, `JwtAuthGuard.canActivate` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` before `verifyToken` and throws when the shared bucket is blocked (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–115). One hundred requests with a forged Bearer that uses the standard HS256 header write the same block key for 300 seconds. Ordinary traffic does the same once the whole user base exceeds 100 authenticated calls in one minute. RS256 Firebase tokens share `eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1`, a second global bucket. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (278); `docs/SSOT/SRS/03-non-functional-requirements.md` (§3.1) -> Action: Same as the plant bullet: key on the verified user id after `verifyToken`.

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-25).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` returns refresh-token keys (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` → `GET /redis-test/get/refresh_token/<sessionId>` → `POST /auth/refresh` mints an access token that copies `payload.roles`. `POST /redis-test/set` and `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` overwrite or delete refresh, blacklist, and cache keys. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` on any deployed environment; never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the Redis instance that stores refresh tokens.

 * **Unauthenticated guest read-receipt forge / unread wipe (2026-09-16, re-verified 2026-09-25).** `OptionalAuthGuard` always returns true (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 338). `POST /api/chat/conversations/:conversationId/read-all` sets `authenticatedUserId = req.user?.userId || body?.user_id` (679). With no JWT, a body user id that is a participant inserts `message_read_receipts` for every unread message. `POST /api/chat/messages/:messageId/read` uses the same fallback (759). Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization` → `POST /api/chat/conversations/<id>/read-all` `{ "user_id": "<victim>" }`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (45–46, 671–743, 751–812); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (308–338) -> Action: Require JWT on mark-read; bind the reader to `req.user.userId`; delete the body `user_id` fallback.

## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **`GET /rate-limit/stats` lists every limiter key with no auth (2026-09-24, re-verified 2026-09-25).** `getRateLimitStats` runs `KEYS rate_limit:*` and `KEYS blocked:*` and returns the key strings (`rate-limit.service.ts` 238–256; controller 213–221). Identifiers embedded in those keys (peer addresses, JOSE prefixes, whatever `/custom` stored) are readable by anyone. `GET /rate-limit/status` answers the same question for a chosen identifier and rule type (124–141). Recommendation: Remove both routes from deployed builds.

 * **Rate limiter fails open when Redis errors.** `checkRateLimit` returns `allowed: true` if the block read or the counter read throws (`rate-limit.service.ts` 87–89, 106–111). A Redis blip disables both the JOSE bucket and the login block. Recommendation: Fail closed on auth routes when the limiter cannot be read.

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics.** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` for `CURRENT_DATE` and clears stats caches (373–401). `POST /api/stats/increment` uses `AdminAuthGuard`. Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token, or drop the public increment.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s posts and follows (776–782) and drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT and bind the viewer to `req.user.userId`.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` and only then flips the ride to `full`. It does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `popular-collections` and `cache-stats`. Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized routes.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified and not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent (0 matches under `apps/`). Public feed returns author `id`, `name`, and `avatar_url`. Recommendation: Add the column and the feed projection; do not treat that as a drive-by security hotfix.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log / record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `userId` from the JWT and then insert any `challengeId`. `GET reset-logs/all` and `GET record-breaks/all` are scoped to `CurrentUser()` (548–571, 629–652). Recommendation: Insert only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws (123–125), and the inner `catch` tries Firebase (126–133). An HS256 refresh token does not verify as a Firebase ID token. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; fall back to Firebase only when signature verification fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. The header `alg` is not read; verification always uses HMAC-SHA256, so `none` / RS256 confusion does not apply to this verifier. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check, and still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** The catch returns `details: error?.message`. Sync user/all and admin-tables handlers do the same. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log details server-side.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL (75). Autocomplete encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register / resolve-id).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `email OR firebase_uid OR google_id` using body `firebaseUid` (723–746), updates identity columns (773–784), and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only the verified Google `sub` or verified email.

 * **`POST /auth/register` returns `Email already registered` (415–418)** despite an anti-enumeration comment. `GET /auth/check-email` already exposes existence by design. Recommendation: Return a generic result and throttle the check.

 * **Web refresh tokens sit in AsyncStorage.** `tokenManager.web.ts` writes `auth_access_token` and `auth_refresh_token` through AsyncStorage, which is `localStorage` on web. Recommendation: Keep the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie on web; leave native SecureStore as it is.

 * **ClosedRoute still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and `user?: any`.** File: `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx`. Recommendation: Use the shared logger and drop the inline `require`.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports). `orderByClause` stays an allowlisted switch.

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`. Hierarchy permission policy lives in the service, but the HTTP layer never supplies the authenticated subject, so the policy cannot see the caller.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controller.** Chat binds JWT conversation lists to self and still dumps any inbox for guests; mark-read falls back to body `user_id`. Community challenges bind PUT/DELETE to the creator and still ignore `is_public` on list, get, and join. Posts hide hidden status on the public feed only, and like/comment writes persist `body.user_id`. Stats admin-gates `analytics/users` and `increment` and leaves `details/:statType` on `JwtAuthGuard` and `track-visit` public. `setManager` checks admin only when a requester id is supplied; `manageHierarchy` does not check admin at all. `SessionController` is registered in every environment, and its login limiter is the same Redis map an anonymous stress-test writes. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so the committed dev Railway template ships Redis `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL`. `JwtAuthGuard` applies one rate-limit bucket to every HS256 caller, and the unguarded rate-limit controller can write that same bucket.

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; personal challenges scope timers and reset-log reads to `CurrentUser()`; `NotificationsController.validateOwnership` gates mark-read and delete; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds the session user; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2 once the shared limiter allows the call; CRM PATCH interpolates hardcoded column names; community-challenge `ORDER BY` uses an allowlist plus `pg-format` `%I`; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/`; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`; dedicated-item and personal-challenge updates go through class-validator DTOs, so extra JSON keys do not become SQL identifiers. Collections names are checked against `ALLOWED_COLLECTIONS` before SQL.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox.

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Unauthenticated one-request lockout of password-verified `/session/login` (2026-09-24).** `RateLimitController` has no `UseGuards`. `POST /rate-limit/stress-test` loops `checkRateLimit(identifier, ruleType)` up to 50 times and defaults `identifier` to `@Ip()` (`rate-limit.controller.ts` 59–84). The built-in `login` rule allows 5 requests per 15 minutes and then sets `blockDurationMs` to 30 minutes (`rate-limit.service.ts` 36–40). The sixth call writes `blocked:login:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `POST /session/login` reads that key with the same `@Ip()` before `argon2.verify` (`session.controller.ts` 42–65, 96) and returns "Too many login attempts". No `trust proxy` setting exists under `apps/api`, so `@Ip()` is the immediate TCP peer. Behind the committed Railway proxy, every client of that process shares the peer, and one stress-test locks session login for all of them. The response body includes the identifier, so the caller learns the shared address. `POST /rate-limit/custom` can plant the same key for an attacker-chosen TTL (`requests: 0`). `SessionController` is registered in every environment (`app.module.ts` 97). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (59–117, 233–248); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (36–40, 82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (42–130); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (97) -> Action: Do not mount `RateLimitController` on deployed builds. Count login failures per account after a password check, not per raw peer address. Set `trust proxy` only for a proxy you trust, and still do not let anonymous callers choose `ruleType` or `identifier`.

 * **Unauthenticated one-shot plant of the shared JOSE JWT lockout (2026-09-23, re-verified 2026-09-24).** `POST /rate-limit/custom` forwards `body.identifier`, `body.rule`, and `body.customKey` into `applyCustomRateLimit`, which sets the Redis rule type to `customKey` (`rate-limit.service.ts` 269–275). `checkRateLimit` stores blocks at `blocked:<ruleType>:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `JwtAuthGuard` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` under rule type `api_access` before signature verification (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 97–114). Compact HS256 headers from `jwt.service.ts` (278) start with `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1`. Concrete trigger: `POST /rate-limit/custom` with `{ "identifier": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1", "customKey": "api_access", "rule": { "requests": 0, "windowMs": 60000, "blockDurationMs": 86400000 } }` and no `Authorization`. `requests: 0` makes `validRequests.length >= rule.requests` true on the first call. Every later HS256 access token then receives `UnauthorizedException("Rate limit exceeded")`. `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can delete that block with no auth. NFR §3.1 currently requires “per token prefix”; that sentence is the defect (SRS §10.3). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (20–21, 151–168, 233–248); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141, 181–191, 269–275); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (276–291) -> Action: Remove `RateLimitController` from deployed builds or require admin JWT; ignore client `customKey` and cap `blockDurationMs`; change §3.1 so the limit is per verified caller after `verifyToken`; keep forged-token abuse on a separate IP bucket.

 * **Shared JOSE-header rate-limit lockout on every JWT route (2026-09-22, re-verified 2026-09-24).** Independent of the plant above, `JwtAuthGuard.canActivate` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` before `verifyToken` and throws when the shared bucket is blocked (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–115). One hundred requests with a forged Bearer that uses the standard HS256 header write the same block key for 300 seconds. Ordinary traffic does the same once the whole user base exceeds 100 authenticated calls in one minute. RS256 Firebase tokens share `eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1`, a second global bucket. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (278); `docs/SSOT/SRS/03-non-functional-requirements.md` (§3.1) -> Action: Same as the plant bullet: key on the verified user id after `verifyToken`.

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-24).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` returns refresh-token keys (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` → `GET /redis-test/get/refresh_token/<sessionId>` → `POST /auth/refresh` mints an access token that copies `payload.roles`. `POST /redis-test/set` and `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` overwrite or delete refresh, blacklist, and cache keys. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` on any deployed environment; never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the Redis instance that stores refresh tokens.

CASCADE`.** `ensurePostsTable` (used from post routes) drops `posts` when legacy columns are detected (78), plus likes/comments (309, 373–374). `tasks-schema.service.ts` (41) can drop `posts`. `DatabaseInit` drops donations/rides on startup (568, 670) when it treats the schema as legacy. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (78, 309, 373–374); `apps/api/src/tasks/tasks-schema.service.ts` (41); `apps/api/src/database/database.init.ts` (568, 670) -> Action: Never DROP on a request path; gate destructive DDL behind an explicit offline migration.

 * **JWT refresh copies stale `payload.roles`.** `refreshAccessToken` copies `payload.roles` (161) and does not reload `user_profiles.roles`. Combined with the redis-test harvest, elevated roles survive demotion for the refresh TTL (30 days). SRS §2.1.4 expects a reload. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (146–177) -> Action: Reload roles from the database on refresh; rotate refresh tokens.

 * **Firebase JWKS accepts any project when the env project id is unset.** `resolveFirebaseProjectIdForJwks` derives the project id from the token `aud` and only rejects a mismatch when `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is set (`firebase-admin.service.ts` 150–184, 191–199). - File: `apps/api/src/auth/services/firebase-admin.service.ts` -> Action: Require a configured project id and reject tokens whose `aud` does not match.

 * **Google `/auth/google` access-token fallback.** If `idToken` verification fails, the handler fetches Google userinfo with a client-supplied `accessToken` and provisions a login with `emailVerified: true` hardcoded. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/auth.controller.ts` (588–698) -> Action: Accept only verified Google/Firebase ID tokens.

 * **ThrottlerModule is not a global guard; `/api/users/login` is unthrottled.** `ThrottlerModule.forRoot` is imported (`app.module.ts` 72–77) and there is no `APP_GUARD`. `UsersController.login` has no `@Throttle`. `AuthController` uses `ThrottlerGuard` plus `@Throttle({ limit: 5 })`. - File: `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (72–77); `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (116–118) -> Action: Register `ThrottlerGuard` as `APP_GUARD`; throttle `/api/users/login` and `resolve-id`.

## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **`GET /rate-limit/stats` lists every limiter key with no auth (2026-09-24).** `getRateLimitStats` runs `KEYS rate_limit:*` and `KEYS blocked:*` and returns the key strings (`rate-limit.service.ts` 238–256; controller 213–221). Identifiers embedded in those keys (peer addresses, JOSE prefixes, whatever `/custom` stored) are readable by anyone. Recommendation: Remove the route from deployed builds.

 * **Rate limiter fails open when Redis errors.** `checkRateLimit` returns `allowed: true` if the block read or the counter read throws (`rate-limit.service.ts` 87–89, 106–111). A Redis blip disables both the JOSE bucket and the login block. Recommendation: Fail closed on auth routes when the limiter cannot be read.

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics.** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` for `CURRENT_DATE` and clears stats caches (373–401). `POST /api/stats/increment` uses `AdminAuthGuard`. Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token, or drop the public increment.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s posts and follows (776–782) and drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT and bind the viewer to `req.user.userId`.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` and only then flips the ride to `full`. It does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `popular-collections` and `cache-stats`. Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized routes.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified and not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent (0 matches under `apps/`). Public feed returns author `id`, `name`, and `avatar_url`. Recommendation: Add the column and the feed projection; do not treat that as a drive-by security hotfix.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log / record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `userId` from the JWT and then insert any `challengeId`. Recommendation: Insert only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws (123–125), and the inner `catch` tries Firebase (126–133). An HS256 refresh token does not verify as a Firebase ID token. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; fall back to Firebase only when signature verification fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. The header `alg` is not read; verification always uses HMAC-SHA256, so `none` / RS256 confusion does not apply to this verifier. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check, and still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** The catch returns `details: error?.message`. Sync user/all and admin-tables handlers do the same. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log details server-side.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL (75). Autocomplete encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register / resolve-id).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `email OR firebase_uid OR google_id` using body `firebaseUid` (723–746), updates identity columns (773–784), and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only the verified Google `sub` or verified email.

 * **`POST /auth/register` returns `Email already registered` (415–418)** despite an anti-enumeration comment. `GET /auth/check-email` already exposes existence by design. Recommendation: Return a generic result and throttle the check.

 * **Web refresh tokens sit in AsyncStorage.** `tokenManager.web.ts` writes `auth_access_token` and `auth_refresh_token` through AsyncStorage, which is `localStorage` on web. Recommendation: Keep the refresh token in an HttpOnly cookie on web; leave native SecureStore as it is.

 * **ClosedRoute still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and `user?: any`.** File: `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx`. Recommendation: Use the shared logger and drop the inline `require`.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports). `orderByClause` stays an allowlisted switch.

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813), `rides.controller.ts` (779). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controller.** Chat binds JWT conversation lists to self and still dumps any inbox for guests; mark-read falls back to body `user_id`. Community challenges bind PUT/DELETE to the creator and still ignore `is_public` on list, get, and join. Posts hide hidden status on the public feed only, and like/comment writes persist `body.user_id`. Stats admin-gates `increment` and leaves `track-visit` public. `SessionController` is registered in every environment, and its login limiter is the same Redis map an anonymous stress-test writes. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so the committed dev Railway template ships Redis `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL`. `JwtAuthGuard` applies one rate-limit bucket to every HS256 caller, and the unguarded rate-limit controller can write that same bucket.

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; personal challenges scope timers to `CurrentUser()`; `NotificationsController.validateOwnership` gates mark-read and delete; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds the session user; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2 once the shared limiter allows the call; CRM PATCH interpolates hardcoded column names; community-challenge `ORDER BY` uses an allowlist plus `pg-format` `%I`; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/`; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`; dedicated-item and personal-challenge updates go through class-validator DTOs, so extra JSON keys do not become SQL identifiers.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox.
