## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Unauthenticated one-shot plant of the shared JOSE JWT lockout (2026-09-23).** `RateLimitController` has no `UseGuards`. `POST /rate-limit/custom` forwards `body.identifier`, `body.rule`, and `body.customKey` into `applyCustomRateLimit`, which sets the Redis rule type to `customKey` (`rate-limit.service.ts` 269–275). `checkRateLimit` stores blocks at `blocked:<ruleType>:<identifier>` (82–83, 120–129). `JwtAuthGuard` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` under rule type `api_access` before signature verification (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 97–114). Compact HS256 headers from `jwt.service.ts` (278) start with `eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1`. Concrete trigger: `POST /rate-limit/custom` with `{ "identifier": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1", "customKey": "api_access", "rule": { "requests": 0, "windowMs": 60000, "blockDurationMs": 86400000 } }` and no `Authorization`. `requests: 0` makes `validRequests.length >= rule.requests` true on the first call, so Redis stores `blocked:api_access:eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1` for the supplied TTL. Every later HS256 access token then receives `UnauthorizedException("Rate limit exceeded")` on every `JwtAuthGuard` route. The same prefix lockout still happens from 100 forged or real Bearer calls (5-minute block written by the guard). `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` can delete that block with no auth. NFR §3.1 currently requires “per token prefix”; that sentence is the defect (SRS §10.3). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` (20–21, 151–168, 233–248); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141, 181–191, 269–275); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (276–291) -> Action: Remove `RateLimitController` from deployed builds or require admin JWT; ignore client `customKey` and cap `blockDurationMs`; change §3.1 so the limit is per verified caller after `verifyToken`; keep forged-token abuse on a separate IP bucket.

 * **Shared JOSE-header rate-limit lockout on every JWT route (2026-09-22, re-verified 2026-09-23).** Independent of the plant above, `JwtAuthGuard.canActivate` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` before `verifyToken` and throws when the shared bucket is blocked (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–115). One hundred requests with `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.x.y` (garbage signature) write the same block key for 300 seconds. Ordinary traffic does the same once the whole user base exceeds 100 authenticated calls in one minute. RS256 Firebase tokens share `eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1`, a second global bucket. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (278); `docs/SSOT/SRS/03-non-functional-requirements.md` (§3.1) -> Action: Same as the plant bullet: key on the verified user id after `verifyToken`.

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-23).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` returns refresh-token keys (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` → `GET /redis-test/get/refresh_token/<sessionId>` → `POST /auth/refresh` mints an access token that copies `payload.roles`. `POST /redis-test/set` and `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` overwrite or delete refresh, blacklist, and cache keys. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` on any deployed environment; never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the Redis instance that stores refresh tokens.

 * **Unauthenticated guest read-receipt forge / unread wipe (2026-09-16, re-verified 2026-09-23).** `OptionalAuthGuard` always returns true (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 338). `POST /api/chat/conversations/:conversationId/read-all` sets `authenticatedUserId = req.user?.userId || body?.user_id` (679). With no JWT, a body user id that is a participant inserts `message_read_receipts` for every unread message. `POST /api/chat/messages/:messageId/read` uses the same fallback (759). Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization` → `POST /api/chat/conversations/<id>/read-all` `{ "user_id": "<victim>" }`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (45–46, 671–743, 751–812); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (308–338) -> Action: Require JWT on mark-read; bind the reader to `req.user.userId`; delete the body `user_id` fallback.

 * **Unauthenticated guest conversation roster harvest (2026-09-15, re-verified 2026-09-23).** JWT callers on `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/:userId` are bound to self (257–266). The guest `else` (267–269) returns `cc.*` plus last-message plaintext. Guest `GET /conversations/<id>/messages` (378–387) selects by id with no participant check. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (246–330, 378–387) -> Action: Require JWT; bind `:userId` to `req.user.userId`; delete the guest branch.

 * **Unauthenticated Redis session-key harvest + session-blob PII (2026-09-14, re-verified 2026-09-23).** `SessionController` has no `UseGuards`. `GET /session/stats` (235–249) returns every `session:*` key. `GET /session/validate/{sessionId}` (136–153) and `GET /session/protected` (256–299) return the full blob. `DELETE /session/logout-all/<userId>` can then drop those sessions. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (136–299) -> Action: Remove `/session` from deployed builds or require admin JWT; do not return raw keys or full session blobs.

 * **JWT-gated social-engagement actor spoof (2026-09-13, re-verified 2026-09-23).** `POST /api/posts/:postId/like` (1343–1353), `POST /api/posts/:postId/comments`, and `POST /api/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId/like` persist `body.user_id`. Any valid JWT can like or comment as another user. Post DELETE binds `getSessionUserId(req)`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (1343–1396, 1573–1643, 2152–2209) -> Action: Bind actors to `req.user.userId`; reject a mismatched body `user_id`.

 * **Private community-challenge join/write ignores `is_public` (2026-09-11, re-verified 2026-09-23).** The public filter applies only when `creator_id` is omitted (232–238). `GET :id` returns the challenge and roster with no public/membership check (496–546). `POST :id/join` selects only `id, is_active` (574–616). Contrast: `PUT :id` / `DELETE :id` require the creator (908–1072). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/community-group-challenges.controller.ts` -> Action: Keep the public filter unless the caller is the creator or an admin; reject join when `is_public = false` unless invited.

 * **Unauthenticated identifier-only account takeover via `POST /api/users/resolve-id`.** No `JwtAuthGuard`. A known email, `google_id`, or `firebase_uid` looks up `user_profiles`, may link caller-supplied identifiers, then mints a JWT pair (`user-auth.service.ts` 270–342, 423–433). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (183–188); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` -> Action: Remove token minting from resolve-id; require a verified ID token; never link identifiers from an unauthenticated body.

 * **Password-optional `/api/users/login` + unauthenticated register Firebase UID bind.** `loginUser` verifies argon2 only when both `password` and `password_hash` are truthy (223–231). ## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Rate limiter fails open when Redis errors.** `checkRateLimit` returns `allowed: true` if the block read or the counter read throws (`rate-limit.service.ts` 87–89, 106–111). A Redis blip disables both the JOSE bucket and the plant. Recommendation: Fail closed on auth routes when the limiter cannot be read.

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics.** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` for `CURRENT_DATE` and clears stats caches (373–401). `POST /api/stats/increment` uses `AdminAuthGuard`. Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token, or drop the public increment.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s posts and follows (776–782) and drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT and bind the viewer to `req.user.userId`.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` and only then flips the ride to `full`. It does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `popular-collections` and `cache-stats`. Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized routes.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified and not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent (0 matches under `apps/`). Public feed returns author `id`, `name`, and `avatar_url`. Recommendation: Add the column and the feed projection; do not treat that as a drive-by security hotfix.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log / record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `userId` from the JWT and then insert any `challengeId`. Recommendation: Insert only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws (123–125), and the inner `catch` tries Firebase (126–133). An HS256 refresh token does not verify as a Firebase ID token. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; fall back to Firebase only when signature verification fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. The header `alg` is not read; verification always uses HMAC-SHA256, so `none` / RS256 confusion does not apply to this verifier. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check, and still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** The catch returns `details: error?.message`. Sync user/all and admin-tables handlers do the same. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log details server-side.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL (75). Autocomplete encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register / resolve-id).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `email OR firebase_uid OR google_id` using body `firebaseUid` (723–746), updates identity columns (773–784), and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only the verified Google `sub` or verified email.

 * **`POST /auth/register` returns `Email already registered` (415–418)** despite an anti-enumeration comment. `GET /auth/check-email` already exposes existence by design. Recommendation: Return a generic result and throttle the check.

 * **ClosedRoute still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and `user?: any`.** File: `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx`. Recommendation: Use the shared logger and drop the inline `require`.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports). `orderByClause` stays an allowlisted switch.

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813), `rides.controller.ts` (779). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controller.** Chat binds JWT conversation lists to self and still dumps any inbox for guests; mark-read falls back to body `user_id`. Community challenges bind PUT/DELETE to the creator and still ignore `is_public` on list, get, and join. Posts hide hidden status on the public feed only, and like/comment writes persist `body.user_id`. Stats admin-gates `increment` and leaves `track-visit` public. `SessionController` is registered in every environment. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so the committed dev Railway template ships Redis `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL`. `JwtAuthGuard` applies one rate-limit bucket to every HS256 caller, and the unguarded rate-limit controller can write that same bucket.

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; personal challenges scope timers to `CurrentUser()`; `NotificationsController.validateOwnership` gates mark-read and delete; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds the session user; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2; CRM PATCH interpolates hardcoded column names; community-challenge `ORDER BY` uses an allowlist plus `pg-format` `%I`; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/`; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox.

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Shared JOSE-header rate-limit lockout on every JWT route (2026-09-22).** `JwtAuthGuard.canActivate` rate-limits `token.substring(0, 16)` before signature verification and throws `UnauthorizedException("Rate limit exceeded")` when the shared bucket is blocked (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 96–115, block written in `rate-limit.service.ts` 120–131). Compact HS256 tokens from `jwt.service.ts` (278) all start with the same 16-character JOSE header. Concrete trigger: 100 requests to any guarded route (for example `GET /api/notifications`) with `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.x.y` — the signature can be garbage. Redis then stores `blocked:api_access:` plus that prefix for 300 seconds, and every legitimate HS256 access token receives 401 on every `JwtAuthGuard` route. The same lockout happens from ordinary traffic once the whole user base exceeds 100 authenticated calls in one minute. NFR §3.1 currently requires “per token prefix”; amend that sentence, then key the bucket on the verified user id and count invalid bearers by client IP. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–134); `apps/api/src/auth/services/rate-limit.service.ts` (82–141); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (278); `docs/SSOT/SRS/03-non-functional-requirements.md` (§3.1) -> Action: Change §3.1 so the limit is per verified caller after `verifyToken`; do not use the JOSE header as the Redis identifier; keep forged-token abuse on a separate IP bucket.

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-22).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` returns refresh-token keys (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` returns the stored refresh JWT. ## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics (still not a data-leak).** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` for `CURRENT_DATE` and clears stats caches (373–401). `POST /api/stats/increment` uses `AdminAuthGuard`. Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token, or drop the public increment.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s posts and follows (776–782) and drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT and bind the viewer to `req.user.userId`.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` and only then flips the ride to `full`. It does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `popular-collections` and `cache-stats`. Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized routes.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified and not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent (0 matches under `apps/`; SRS §10). Public feed returns author `id`, `name`, and `avatar_url`. Recommendation: Add the column and the feed projection; do not treat that as a drive-by security hotfix.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log / record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `userId` from the JWT and then insert any `challengeId`. Recommendation: Insert only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws (123–125), and the inner `catch` tries Firebase (126–133). An HS256 refresh token does not verify as a Firebase ID token. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; fall back to Firebase only when signature verification fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after a length check, and still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** The catch returns `details: error?.message`. Recommendation: Return a generic error and log details server-side.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL (75). Autocomplete encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register / resolve-id).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `email OR firebase_uid OR google_id` using body `firebaseUid` (723–746), updates identity columns (773–784), and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only the verified Google `sub` or verified email.

 * **`POST /auth/register` returns `Email already registered` (415–418)** despite an anti-enumeration comment. `GET /auth/check-email` already exposes existence by design. Recommendation: Return a generic result and throttle the check.

 * **ClosedRoute still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and `user?: any`.** File: `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx`. Recommendation: Use the shared logger and drop the inline `require`.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). The target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders plus React Native screens. `packages/` still only contains `config-eslint`. The closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, and `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest or `pg` imports).

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL and policy.** Largest API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813), `rides.controller.ts` (779). `items-delivery.service.ts` remains under `controllers/`.

 * **Privilege checks disagree inside the same controller.** Chat binds JWT conversation lists to self and still dumps any inbox for guests; mark-read falls back to body `user_id`. Community challenges bind PUT/DELETE to the creator and still ignore `is_public` on list, get, and join. Posts hide hidden status on the public feed only, and like/comment writes persist `body.user_id`. Stats admin-gates `increment` and leaves `track-visit` public. `SessionController` is registered in every environment. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"`, so the committed dev Railway template ships Redis `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL`. `JwtAuthGuard` applies one rate-limit bucket to every HS256 caller because the identifier is the shared JOSE prefix, which is what NFR §3.1 currently asks for.

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group challenges bind the creator on create/join/entry and use `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; personal challenges scope timers to `CurrentUser()`; `NotificationsController.validateOwnership` gates mark-read and delete; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; sync user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds the session user; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; `/session/login` requires argon2; CRM PATCH interpolates hardcoded column names; `WebViewScreen` loads the constant `https://www.jgive.com/` and ignores the unused deep-link `url` parser; admin tables sit behind `AdminAuthGuard`.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified and not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists and there is no `/api/operator/*` module. Anonymity and matching-case tables remain SRS §10 gaps. NFR §3.2 says admin access is role-based only, while register/login still promote the committed fallback mailbox — that conflict stays open (see the root-admin bullet above).

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-20).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` calls `redis.keys` and returns every JWT refresh-token key (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` (74–91) returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: with Redis up on that service, `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` → `GET /redis-test/get/refresh_token/<sessionId>` → `POST /auth/refresh` `{ "refreshToken": "<stolen>" }` mints a new access token copying `payload.roles`. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=*` also dumps `session:*`, `blacklisted_token:*`, `user_sessions:*`, and cache keys. `POST /redis-test/set` overwrites any key; `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` deletes refresh tokens or blacklist entries. Distinct from 2026-09-14: `GET /session/stats` only returns `session:*` demo blobs, not `/auth` refresh JWTs. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 123–130, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` in any deployed environment (gate on an explicit local-only flag, not `NODE_ENV`); never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the shared Redis used for refresh tokens and sessions.

 * **Unauthenticated guest read-receipt forge / unread wipe (2026-09-16, re-verified 2026-09-20).** Class `OptionalAuthGuard` always returns true (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 338). `POST /api/chat/conversations/:conversationId/read-all` (671–743) sets `authenticatedUserId = req.user?.userId || body?.user_id` (679). With no JWT, the body value is resolved and, if that id is in `participants`, the handler INSERTs `message_read_receipts` for every unread message. `POST /api/chat/messages/:messageId/read` (751–812) uses the same fallback (759). Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` yields a victim UUID/email; `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization` (09-15) returns conversation ids; `POST /api/chat/conversations/<id>/read-all` `{ "user_id": "<victim>" }` with no JWT marks the victim’s inbox read. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 671–743, 751–812); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (338) -> Action: Require JWT on mark-read; bind the reader exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete the body `user_id` fallback.

 * **Unauthenticated guest conversation roster harvest (auth inversion) (2026-09-15, re-verified 2026-09-20).** JWT callers on `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/:userId` (246–330) are bound to self (257–266). The `else` branch (267–269) runs when `req.user` is missing and dumps `cc.*` plus last-message plaintext for any UUID/email. Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization`. Follow with guest `GET /conversations/<id>/messages` (378–387) which looks up `WHERE id = $1` with no `ANY(participants)` check. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 246–330, 378–387); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (338) -> Action: Require JWT on conversation list and message reads; bind `:userId` exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete the guest `else` path.

 * **Unauthenticated Redis session-key harvest + session-blob PII (2026-09-14, re-verified 2026-09-20).** `SessionController` has no `UseGuards`. `GET /session/stats` (235–249) returns every `session:*` key. `GET /session/validate/{sessionId}` (136–153) and `GET /session/protected` (256–299, `session-id` header) return the full blob (`userId`, `email`, username, IP, UA). Concrete trigger: `GET /session/stats` → for each key, `GET /session/validate/<id>` harvests every live user’s email and UUID; `DELETE /session/logout-all/<userId>` then force-logs them out. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (136–249, 256–299) -> Action: Remove `/session` from production builds (or require admin JWT); never return raw Redis keys or full session blobs; bind logout to the caller’s own session.

## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Unauthenticated `POST /api/stats/track-visit` inflates production metrics (noted 2026-09-20, not first-classed as critical).** No guard. Increments `community_stats.site_visits` for `CURRENT_DATE` and clears stats caches (373–401). Contrast: `POST /api/stats/increment` correctly uses `AdminAuthGuard` (403–405). Recommendation: Require a bot-resistant token or drop the public increment; keep only first-party analytics writes.

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s own posts and the people they follow (776–782) and the same id drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT; bind viewer exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete or auth-gate the likes/check and `viewer_id` query.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` then only flips the ride to `full` after the fact — it does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Concurrent books can oversell. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros, hiding failures. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`, so `GET /api/items-delivery/requests` hits `getItemById("requests")`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `GET popular-collections` / `GET cache-stats` (those return 400 Invalid collection). Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized `:id` / `:collection`.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified but not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent from posts DDL (SRS §10; repo-wide search this run: 0 matches under `apps/`). Public feed returns author `id` / `name` / `avatar_url` for every post. Recommendation: Add the column + feed/by-id projection per SRS; do not treat this as a new product feature in a security hotfix PR.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log / record-break `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` (502–546) and `POST /api/challenges/record-breaks` (584–627) overwrite `createDto.userId` from the JWT then INSERT any `challengeId` with no `challenges.user_id` match. Recommendation: INSERT only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws `UnauthorizedException` (123–125), which the inner `catch` treats as “try Firebase” (126–133). An HS256 refresh token fails Google JWKS, so this is not currently exploitable; it is a confused control-flow that can hide real JWT errors behind `Invalid Firebase token: …`. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; only fall back to Firebase when signature verification itself fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. Combined with the committed `JWT_SECRET` in `railway.toml.dev`, this is secondary to secret rotation. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after length-checking; still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** Catch returns `{ success: false, error: "Failed to get user", details: error?.message }`. Production `ValidationPipe` `disableErrorMessages` does not cover this hand-rolled envelope. Recommendation: Return a generic error; log the details server-side only.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL without `encodeURIComponent` (75). Autocomplete correctly encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`; consider allowlisting Place ID shape.

 * **ClosedRoute task-type / duplicate handling.** `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx` still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and a loose `user?: any` prop. Recommendation: Use the shared logger; unify closed-content type tags; drop the inline `require`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register/`resolve-id`, not newly first-classed).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `WHERE email = $1 OR firebase_uid = $2 OR google_id = $3 LIMIT 1` with body `firebaseUid` (723–746), then UPDATEs that row’s `firebase_uid`/`google_id` (773–784) and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only on verified Google `sub` / verified email; never accept a client `firebaseUid`; do not UPDATE identity columns from the body.

 * **`POST /auth/register` contradicts its anti-enumeration comment.** Handler returns `Email already registered` (415–418). Low severity next to the explicit `GET /auth/check-email` existence oracle. Recommendation: Return a generic success/failure; keep existence checks admin-only or heavily throttled.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). Target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders + RN screens; `packages/` still only `config-eslint`. Closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest/pg imports).

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL + policy.** Worst API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813), `rides.controller.ts` (779). `items-delivery.service.ts` is misplaced under `controllers/`.

Posts hide on the public feed only; likes/comments writes are JWT-gated but bind `body.user_id`. Users JWT-gates follow/hierarchy writes but leaves `:id/activities` and `:id/stats` public. Stats admin-gates `analytics/users` and `increment` but JWT-only-gates `details/:statType` and leaves `track-visit` public. Rides has no guards at all. `SessionController` is registered in every environment despite DEMO/TEST file comments. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"` rather than an explicit local-only flag, so the committed dev Railway template ships live Redis KEYS/GET/SET/DEL (2026-09-17).

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group-challenges binds creator from JWT on create/join/entry and uses `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; ChallengesController scopes personal timers to `CurrentUser()`; NotificationsController.`validateOwnership`; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; SyncController user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds session user without body fallback; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; authenticated `GET conversations/user/:userId` already denies cross-user reads (do not delete that branch — apply it to guests too); `/session/login` correctly requires argon2 (contrast `/api/users/login`); CRM PATCH uses hardcoded column names (not `Object.keys`); mobile `WebViewScreen` does not take a caller-controlled URL.

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-19).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (line 25), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` calls `redis.keys` and returns every JWT refresh-token key (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` (74–91) returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: with Redis up on that service, `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` → `GET /redis-test/get/refresh_token/<sessionId>` → `POST /auth/refresh` `{ "refreshToken": "<stolen>" }` mints a new access token copying `payload.roles`. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=*` also dumps `session:*`, `blacklisted_token:*`, `user_sessions:*`, and cache keys. `POST /redis-test/set` overwrites any key; `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` deletes refresh tokens or blacklist entries. Distinct from 2026-09-14: `GET /session/stats` only returns `session:*` demo blobs, not `/auth` refresh JWTs. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 123–130, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` in any deployed environment (gate on an explicit local-only flag, not `NODE_ENV`); never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the shared Redis used for refresh tokens and sessions.

 * **Unauthenticated guest read-receipt forge / unread wipe (2026-09-16, re-verified 2026-09-19).** Class `OptionalAuthGuard` always returns true (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 338). `POST /api/chat/conversations/:conversationId/read-all` (671–743) sets `authenticatedUserId = req.user?.userId || body?.user_id` (679). With no JWT, the body value is resolved and, if that id is in `participants`, the handler INSERTs `message_read_receipts` for every unread message. `POST /api/chat/messages/:messageId/read` (751–812) uses the same fallback (759). Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` yields a victim UUID/email; `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization` (09-15) returns conversation ids; `POST /api/chat/conversations/<id>/read-all` `{ "user_id": "<victim>" }` with no JWT marks the victim’s inbox read. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 671–743, 751–812); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (338) -> Action: Require JWT on mark-read; bind the reader exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete the body `user_id` fallback.

 * **Unauthenticated guest conversation roster harvest (auth inversion) (2026-09-15, re-verified 2026-09-19).** JWT callers on `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/:userId` (246–330) are bound to self (257–266). The `else` branch (267–269) runs when `req.user` is missing and dumps `cc.*` plus last-message plaintext for any UUID/email. Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization`. Follow with guest `GET /conversations/<id>/messages` (378–387) which looks up `WHERE id = $1` with no `ANY(participants)` check. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 246–330, 378–387); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (338) -> Action: Require JWT on conversation list and message reads; bind `:userId` exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete the guest `else` path.

 * **Unauthenticated Redis session-key harvest + session-blob PII (2026-09-14, re-verified 2026-09-19).** `SessionController` has no `UseGuards`. `GET /session/stats` (235–249) returns every `session:*` key. `GET /session/validate/{sessionId}` (136–153) and `GET /session/protected` (256–299, `session-id` header) return the full blob (`userId`, `email`, username, IP, UA). Concrete trigger: `GET /session/stats` → for each key, `GET /session/validate/<id>` harvests every live user’s email and UUID; `DELETE /session/logout-all/<userId>` then force-logs them out. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (136–249, 256–299) -> Action: Remove `/session` from production builds (or require admin JWT); never return raw Redis keys or full session blobs; bind logout to the caller’s own session.

 * **JWT-gated social-engagement actor spoof (2026-09-13, re-verified 2026-09-19).** `POST /api/posts/:postId/like` (1343–1396), `POST /api/posts/:postId/comments` (1573–1643), and `POST /api/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId/like` (2152–2209) persist `body.user_id` with no `req.user` bind. Concrete trigger: any valid JWT user A comments as `{ "user_id": "<victim>", "text": "..." }`. Contrast: post DELETE (2626–2663) binds `getSessionUserId(req)`. Complements comment PUT/DELETE spoof (1985–2058). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (1343–1396, 1573–1643, 2152–2209) -> Action: Bind like/comment actors exclusively to `req.user.userId`; reject a mismatched body `user_id`.

 * **Private community-challenge join/write ignores `is_public` (2026-09-11, re-verified 2026-09-19).** Default list applies `AND COALESCE(c.is_public, true) = true` only when `creator_id` is omitted (232–238). `GET :id` (496–546) returns `c.*` + participant roster with no public/membership check. `POST :id/join` (574–616) selects only `id, is_active`. `POST :id/entries` (667–685) accepts any participant. Contrast: `PUT :id` / `DELETE :id` require `creator_id === CurrentUser()` (908–1072). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (183–238, 496–546, 560–631, 651–677) -> Action: Keep the public filter even when `creator_id` is set unless the caller is that creator or an admin; require membership or `is_public` on `GET :id`; reject `join` when `is_public = false` unless invited/creator.

 * **Unauthenticated identifier-only account takeover via `POST /api/users/resolve-id`.** No `JwtAuthGuard`. Supplying a known `email`, `google_id`, or `firebase_uid` looks up `user_profiles`, optionally links caller-supplied identifiers, then mints a full JWT pair.  * **Password-optional `/api/users/login` + unauthenticated register Firebase UID bind.** `loginUser` verifies argon2 only when both `password` and `password_hash` are truthy (223–231); omitted/empty password still returns `{ success: true, data: userResponse }` including `roles` and `phone`. `POST /api/users/register` INSERTs `userData.firebase_uid || userData.id` (139). Combined with resolve-id this is account takeover / identity hijack. - File: `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (97–99, 139, 223–263) -> Action: Fail closed unless a password is supplied and verifies; ignore client `firebase_uid`/`id` on public register.

Root-admin block covers roles/hierarchy only; `password` and `firebase_uid` are still written. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (126–133); `apps/api/src/services/user-profile.service.ts` (18–32, 267, 281–361) -> Action: Bind `:id` to `req.user.userId` unless admin; strip `password`/`roles`/`firebase_uid` from the public DTO.

 * **Unauthenticated user/hierarchy/activity dumps.** `GET /api/users`, `GET :id`, `GET search`, `GET hierarchy/tree`, `GET :id/hierarchy`, `GET eligible-for-promotion/:adminId`, `GET :id/activities`, `GET :id/stats` have no guards. Hierarchy writes are JWT-gated but trust body `requestingAdminId` / `follower_id`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (40–43, 91–108, 121–163, 165–180); `apps/api/src/services/user-follow.service.ts` (6–34) -> Action: Auth-gate directory/hierarchy/activity reads; bind follow/hierarchy actors to `req.user`.

## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s own posts and the people they follow (776–782) and the same id drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT; bind viewer exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete or auth-gate the likes/check and `viewer_id` query.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` then only flips the ride to `full` after the fact — it does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Concurrent books can oversell. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros, hiding failures. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`, so `GET /api/items-delivery/requests` hits `getItemById("requests")`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `GET popular-collections` / `GET cache-stats` (those return 400 Invalid collection). Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized `:id` / `:collection`.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified but not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent from posts DDL (SRS §10; repo-wide search this run: 0 matches under `apps/`). Public feed returns author `id` / `name` / `avatar_url` for every post. Recommendation: Add the column + feed/by-id projection per SRS; do not treat this as a new product feature in a security hotfix PR.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` overwrites `createDto.userId` from the JWT then INSERTs any `challengeId` with no `challenges.user_id` match. Recommendation: INSERT only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws `UnauthorizedException` (123–125), which the inner `catch` treats as “try Firebase” (126–133). An HS256 refresh token fails Google JWKS, so this is not currently exploitable; it is a confused control-flow that can hide real JWT errors behind `Invalid Firebase token: …`. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; only fall back to Firebase when signature verification itself fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. Combined with the committed `JWT_SECRET` in `railway.toml.dev`, this is secondary to secret rotation. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after length-checking; still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** Catch returns `{ success: false, error: "Failed to get user", details: error?.message }`. Production `ValidationPipe` `disableErrorMessages` does not cover this hand-rolled envelope. Recommendation: Return a generic error; log the details server-side only.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL without `encodeURIComponent` (75). Autocomplete correctly encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`; consider allowlisting Place ID shape.

 * **ClosedRoute task-type / duplicate handling.** `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx` still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and a loose `user?: any` prop. Recommendation: Use the shared logger; unify closed-content type tags; drop the inline `require`.

 * **`POST /auth/google` identity OR-lookup (same class as register/`resolve-id`, not newly first-classed).** After a valid Google token, the handler matches `WHERE email = $1 OR firebase_uid = $2 OR google_id = $3 LIMIT 1` with body `firebaseUid` (741–746), then UPDATEs that row’s `firebase_uid`/`google_id` (773–784) and mints tokens (935–951). Recommendation: Match only on verified Google `sub` / verified email; never accept a client `firebaseUid`; do not UPDATE identity columns from the body.

## 🏗️ Architecture & Clean Code

 * **No Domain / Application / Infrastructure folders** under `apps/` or `packages/` (count 0). Target in `docs/SSOT/CODE_QUALITY/layers-and-boundaries.md` is Infrastructure → Application → Domain. The monorepo remains NestJS feature folders + RN screens; `packages/` still only `config-eslint`. Closest pure islands remain `apps/api/src/tasks/task-completion-participants.ts`, `tasks-validation.ts`, `tasks-query-params.ts`, `tasks.types.ts` (no Nest/pg imports).

 * **Fat HTTP layer owns SQL + policy.** Worst API files: `posts.controller.ts` (2741), `stats.controller.ts` (1709), `user-hierarchy.service.ts` (1675), `database.init.ts` (1374), `community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (1097), `chat.controller.ts` (813), `rides.controller.ts` (779). `items-delivery.service.ts` is misplaced under `controllers/`.

 * **Privilege checks are inconsistent inside the same controller (authorization-in-one-file smell).** Chat JWT conversation list binds `:userId` to self while the guest branch dumps any inbox (2026-09-15); JWT send/read checks `ANY(participants)` while the guest branch skips it (378–387) and `createConversation` returns `SELECT *` of an existing DM; mark-read prefers JWT then falls back to body `user_id` (2026-09-16). Community-group-challenges binds JWT on create/join/entry and correctly gates PUT/DELETE to the creator, but list/`GET :id`/join ignore `is_public`. Posts hide on the public feed only; likes/comments writes are JWT-gated but bind `body.user_id`. Users JWT-gates follow/hierarchy writes but leaves `:id/activities` and `:id/stats` public. Stats admin-gates `analytics/users` but JWT-only-gates `details/:statType`. Rides has no guards at all. `SessionController` is registered in every environment despite DEMO/TEST file comments. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"` rather than an explicit local-only flag, so the committed dev Railway template ships live Redis KEYS/GET/SET/DEL (2026-09-17).

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group-challenges binds creator from JWT on create/join/entry and uses `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; ChallengesController scopes personal timers to `CurrentUser()`; NotificationsController.`validateOwnership`; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; SyncController user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds session user without body fallback; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; authenticated `GET conversations/user/:userId` already denies cross-user reads (do not delete that branch — apply it to guests too); `/session/login` correctly requires argon2 (contrast `/api/users/login`); CRM PATCH uses hardcoded column names (not `Object.keys`); mobile `WebViewScreen` does not take a caller-controlled URL.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified, not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists (`jwt-auth.guard.ts`) but there is no `/api/operator/*` module (zero operator controller files). Anonymity + matching-case audit tables remain SRS §10 gaps.

## 🚨 Critical Vulnerabilities

 * **Unauthenticated JWT refresh-token harvest / arbitrary Redis R/W (2026-09-17, re-verified 2026-09-18).** `RedisTestController` has no `UseGuards`. It is registered whenever `NODE_ENV !== "production"` (`app.module.ts` 122). `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` sets `NODE_ENV = "development"` (and `ENVIRONMENT = "development"`), so the controller is mounted on the committed dev Railway template. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` calls `redis.keys` and returns every JWT refresh-token key (`jwt.service.ts` 33, 338–343). `GET /redis-test/get/:key` (74–91) returns the stored refresh JWT. Concrete trigger: with Redis up on that service, `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=refresh_token:*` → `GET /redis-test/get/refresh_token/<sessionId>` → `POST /auth/refresh` `{ "refreshToken": "<stolen>" }` mints a new access token copying `payload.roles`. `GET /redis-test/keys?pattern=*` also dumps `session:*`, `blacklisted_token:*`, `user_sessions:*`, and cache keys. `POST /redis-test/set` overwrites any key; `DELETE /redis-test/delete/:key` deletes refresh tokens or blacklist entries. Distinct from 2026-09-14: `GET /session/stats` only returns `session:*` demo blobs, not `/auth` refresh JWTs. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/redis-test.controller.ts` (16–137); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (122); `apps/api/railway.toml.dev` (25); `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (33, 123–130, 146–177, 338–343) -> Action: Do not register `RedisTestController` in any deployed environment (gate on an explicit local-only flag, not `NODE_ENV`); never expose `KEYS`/`GET`/`SET`/`DEL` on the shared Redis used for refresh tokens and sessions.

 * **Unauthenticated guest read-receipt forge / unread wipe (2026-09-16, re-verified 2026-09-18).** Class `OptionalAuthGuard` always returns true (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 338). `POST /api/chat/conversations/:conversationId/read-all` (671–743) sets `authenticatedUserId = req.user?.userId || body?.user_id` (679). With no JWT, the body value is resolved and, if that id is in `participants`, the handler INSERTs `message_read_receipts` for every unread message. `POST /api/chat/messages/:messageId/read` (751–812) uses the same fallback (759). Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` yields a victim UUID/email; `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization` (09-15) returns conversation ids; `POST /api/chat/conversations/<id>/read-all` `{ "user_id": "<victim>" }` with no JWT marks the victim’s inbox read. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 671–743, 751–812); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (338) -> Action: Require JWT on mark-read; bind the reader exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete the body `user_id` fallback.

 * **Unauthenticated guest conversation roster harvest (auth inversion) (2026-09-15, re-verified 2026-09-18).** JWT callers on `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/:userId` (246–330) are bound to self (257–266). The `else` branch (267–269) runs when `req.user` is missing and dumps `cc.*` plus last-message plaintext for any UUID/email. Concrete trigger: `GET /api/users` → `GET /api/chat/conversations/user/<victim>` with no `Authorization`. Follow with guest `GET /conversations/<id>/messages` (378–387) which looks up `WHERE id = $1` with no `ANY(participants)` check. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 246–330, 378–387); `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (338) -> Action: Require JWT on conversation list and message reads; bind `:userId` exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete the guest `else` path.

 * **Unauthenticated Redis session-key harvest + session-blob PII (2026-09-14, re-verified 2026-09-18).** `SessionController` has no `UseGuards`. `GET /session/stats` (235–249) returns every `session:*` key. `GET /session/validate/{sessionId}` (136–153) and `GET /session/protected` (256–299, `session-id` header) return the full blob (`userId`, `email`, username, IP, UA). Concrete trigger: `GET /session/stats` → for each key, `GET /session/validate/<id>` harvests every live user’s email and UUID; `DELETE /session/logout-all/<userId>` then force-logs them out. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts` (136–249, 256–299) -> Action: Remove `/session` from production builds (or require admin JWT); never return raw Redis keys or full session blobs; bind logout to the caller’s own session.

 * **JWT-gated social-engagement actor spoof (2026-09-13, re-verified 2026-09-18).** `POST /api/posts/:postId/like` (1343–1396), `POST /api/posts/:postId/comments` (1573–1643), and `POST /api/posts/:postId/comments/:commentId/like` (2152–2209) persist `body.user_id` with no `req.user` bind. Concrete trigger: any valid JWT user A comments as `{ "user_id": "<victim>", "text": "..." }`. Contrast: post DELETE (2626–2663) binds `getSessionUserId(req)`. Complements comment PUT/DELETE spoof (1985–2058). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (1343–1396, 1573–1643, 2152–2209) -> Action: Bind like/comment actors exclusively to `req.user.userId`; reject a mismatched body `user_id`.

 * **Private community-challenge join/write ignores `is_public` (2026-09-11, re-verified 2026-09-18).** Default list applies `AND COALESCE(c.is_public, true) = true` only when `creator_id` is omitted (232–238). `GET :id` (496–546) returns `c.*` + participant roster with no public/membership check. `POST :id/join` (574–616) selects only `id, is_active`. `POST :id/entries` (667–685) accepts any participant. Contrast: `PUT :id` / `DELETE :id` require `creator_id === CurrentUser()` (908–1072). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/community-group-challenges.controller.ts` (183–238, 496–546, 560–631, 651–677) -> Action: Keep the public filter even when `creator_id` is set unless the caller is that creator or an admin; require membership or `is_public` on `GET :id`; reject `join` when `is_public = false` unless invited/creator.

 * **Unauthenticated identifier-only account takeover via `POST /api/users/resolve-id`.** No `JwtAuthGuard`. Supplying a known `email`, `google_id`, or `firebase_uid` looks up `user_profiles`, optionally links caller-supplied identifiers, then mints a full JWT pair. Concrete trigger: `POST /api/users/resolve-id` with `{ "email": "<victim>" }` returns tokens with the victim’s `roles`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (183–188); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (270–342) -> Action: Remove token minting from resolve-id; require a verified ID token; never link identifiers from an unauthenticated body.

 * **Primary mobile login accepts email-only (password verification skipped, including empty string).** `POST /api/users/login` verifies argon2 **only when both** `loginData.password` and `user.password_hash` are truthy (223–231). Omitting `password` or sending `password: ""` falls through to `success: true` and returns email, phone, roles, and `parent_manager_id`. `/auth/login` correctly rejects missing hash and invalid passwords. Contrasts SRS §2.1.2. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (116–118); `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (190–263, especially 223–231) -> Action: Always require a non-empty password; fail closed if hash is missing; never return `success: true` without `argon2.verify`.

 * **Unauthenticated root-admin bootstrap via committed fallback email (identity-source split).** `KC_ROOT_ADMIN_EMAIL_FALLBACK` is committed in `kc-root-admin.defaults.ts`. Unauthenticated `POST /api/users/register` with that email sets `initialRoles = ["user", "admin"]`. Unauthenticated `POST /api/users/login` with the same email runs `array_append(roles, 'admin')` **before** the optional password check (212–220). `getRootAdminEmail()` reads only `ROOT_ADMIN_EMAIL` (empty if unset). The PUT role block compares a hardcoded Gmail literal, not the env var. - File: `apps/api/src/config/kc-root-admin.defaults.ts`; `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (101–102, 212–231); `apps/api/src/services/user-profile.service.ts` (52–56, 281–297) -> Action: Single source of truth for root-admin identity; require verified secret/env match plus password; never mutate roles before `argon2.verify`.

 * **Unauthenticated register binds attacker-chosen Firebase UID.** `POST /api/users/register` has no guard. INSERT writes `userData.firebase_uid || userData.id || null`. Password is optional. The victim’s later Firebase ID-token path attaches the attacker’s KC row. - File: `apps/api/src/services/user-auth.service.ts` (97–99, 139) -> Action: Ignore client `firebase_uid`/`id` on public register; require a verified Firebase ID token before binding.

 * **JWT-gated profile mass-assignment + password IDOR (`PUT /api/users/:id`).** `UpdateUserBody` accepts `password`, `roles`, and `firebase_uid`. Controller uses `JwtAuthGuard` only — no ownership check and no `req.user` binding. Lookup matches UUID or email / `firebase_uid` / `google_id`. Root-admin block covers roles/hierarchy only; `password` and `firebase_uid` are still written. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (126–133); `apps/api/src/services/user-profile.service.ts` (18–32, 267, 281–361) -> Action: Bind `:id` to `req.user.userId` unless admin; strip `password`/`roles`/`firebase_uid` from the public DTO.

 * **Unauthenticated user directory and profile PII.** `GET /api/users`, `GET /api/users/:id`, `GET /api/users/search`, and `GET /api/users/stats/summary` have no guards. `getUserById` / `searchUsers` return email, phone, and roles. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (40–43, 101–123, 135–149) -> Action: Require auth (and minimize fields) on list/search/profile/summary reads.

 * **Unauthenticated activity stream is a hidden-post / social-graph / financial discovery oracle (2026-09-08, re-verified 2026-09-18).** `GET /api/users/:id/activities` (152–158) has no `UseGuards` and returns `activity_type` + `activity_data`. Writers persist hide `{post_id}`, follow `{followed_user_id}`, chat `{conversation_id}`, ride `{ride_id, from, to, seats}`, donation `{donation_id, type, amount}`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (152–158); `apps/api/src/services/user-stats.service.ts` (24–47) -> Action: Require JWT + ownership (or admin); redact `activity_data` for non-owners.

 * **Unauthenticated pairwise-DM factory / existence oracle + guest message inject (2026-09-09 / 2026-09-10, re-verified 2026-09-18).** `POST /api/chat/conversations` (107–244): no JWT → body `created_by` used as-is; `SELECT *` of the exact participant set returns or creates the DM. `POST /api/chat/messages` without JWT uses body `sender_id`; conversation lookup is `WHERE id = $1` only vs authenticated `ANY(participants)`. Guest `GET conversations/:id/messages` (378–387) dumps history. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/chat.controller.ts` (46, 107–244, 378–387, 441–569) -> Action: Require JWT on all chat writes and message reads; bind `created_by`/`sender_id` to `req.user`; always enforce `ANY(participants)`.

 * **Client-supplied hierarchy actors + unauthenticated hierarchy tree.** JWT-gated promote/demote/set-manager still trust body `requestingAdminId` / `requestingUserId`; omit or not-found skips the admin check. `POST :id/hierarchy/manage` has no actor field at all. `GET eligible-for-promotion/:adminId`, `GET hierarchy/tree`, and `GET :id/hierarchy` have no guards. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/users.controller.ts` (45–108); `apps/api/src/services/user-hierarchy.service.ts` (492–517, 871–942) -> Action: Bind actor to `req.user`; require `AdminAuthGuard` on manage/promote; fail closed when requester is missing.

 * **Spoofable follow `follower_id`.** `POST`/`DELETE /api/users/:id/follow` are JWT-gated but insert/delete using body `follower_id`, not `req.user.userId`. - File: `apps/api/src/services/user-follow.service.ts` (6–34) -> Action: Bind follower exclusively to the JWT subject.

 * **JWT refresh copies stale `payload.roles` and never reloads DB roles.** `refreshAccessToken` (`jwt.service.ts` 146–177) copies `payload.roles` into the new access token. A revoked admin keeps admin until the refresh token expires (30 days). Combined with `/redis-test` harvest, a stolen refresh token preserves baked-in roles. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/services/jwt.service.ts` (146–177) -> Action: Reload roles from `user_profiles` on refresh; reject refresh if the user is inactive.

 * **Firebase JWKS accepts any project when env project id is unset.** `verifyIdTokenWithPublicJwks` derives `aud` from the token; `resolveFirebaseProjectIdForJwks` only rejects a *different* env project when `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` / service-account `project_id` is set (177–182). If those are empty, any Firebase project’s ID token verifies. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/services/firebase-admin.service.ts` (11–14, 164–200, 242–264) -> Action: Require a configured project id and reject tokens whose `aud` does not match.

 * **Google `/auth/google` access-token fallback.** If `idToken` verification fails, the handler fetches Google userinfo with a client-supplied `accessToken` and provisions/logs in from that profile. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/auth.controller.ts` (588–673) -> Action: Accept only verified Google/Firebase ID tokens; do not treat a bearer access token as login proof.

 * **JwtAuthGuard rate-limit identifier is the shared HS256 token prefix.** `checkRateLimit(token.substring(0, 16), "api_access")` (`jwt-auth.guard.ts` 97–100) is identical for every token signed with the same secret. `ThrottlerModule` is registered (`app.module.ts` 72–77) but there is **no** global `APP_GUARD` for `ThrottlerGuard`. Primary mobile `POST /api/users/login` and `POST /api/users/register` are unthrottled. Unauthenticated `DELETE /rate-limit/clear` and `POST /rate-limit/custom` can clear or plant the shared bucket. - File: `apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts` (96–100); `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (72–77); `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` -> Action: Rate-limit by user id / IP; register `ThrottlerGuard` globally; throttle login/register; admin-gate `/rate-limit/*`.

 * **Unauthenticated ride POST/PUT/DELETE + public driver PII + spoofable actors.** No `UseGuards` on `RidesController`. `POST /` trusts body `driver_id` and can INSERT `user_profiles`. `PUT :id` / `DELETE :id` (695–755) are unauthenticated. `GET /` returns `driver_phone`; `GET :id` returns `driver_phone` + `driver_email`. Booking approval can oversell (505–555). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/rides.controller.ts` -> Action: Require JWT on all ride writes; bind driver/passenger to `req.user`; never INSERT `user_profiles` from an unauthenticated body; `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject oversell; strip phone/email from public GET.

 * **Unauthenticated hidden-post bypass (2026-09-06) and liker roster (2026-09-07), re-verified 2026-09-18.** Public feed filters `(p.status IS NULL OR p.status != 'hidden')` (754). `GET /api/posts/user/:userId` uses `WHERE p.author_id = $1` only. `GET /api/posts/:postId` uses `WHERE p.id = $1` only. `GET :postId/comments` ignores `posts.status`. `GET :postId/likes` and `GET :postId/likes/check/:userId` have no guard and no status join. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (754 vs 1023–1167, 1463–1546) -> Action: Apply the hidden-status predicate on user-posts, by-id, likes, comments, and the activity stream unless the caller is the author or an admin.

 * **Comment PUT/DELETE actor spoof.** JWT-gated `PUT :postId/comments/:commentId` compares ownership to body `user_id` (1985–2014), not `req.user`. `DELETE` uses query `user_id` (2053–2058). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (1975–2058) -> Action: Bind actor to `req.user.userId`.

Knowledge-link `POST /api/donations/knowledge/links` remains public and accepts spoofable `createdByUserId` / `displayName`. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/donations.controller.ts` -> Action: Bind `donor_id` to JWT; require ownership or admin on PUT/DELETE; auth-gate list/by-user/detail; strip donor PII; require JWT (or moderation) on knowledge-link create.

Community-members GET returns `contact_info`; `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` remain unauthenticated writes. CRM `GET /api/crm` runs `SELECT * FROM crm_contacts`; writes are also unauthenticated. Rate-limit `POST custom` / `DELETE clear` / `POST stress-test` are unauthenticated. Redis-test remains in this unguarded set (JWT harvest first-classed separately). - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/items-delivery.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/items/dedicated-items.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/auth/controllers/session.controller.ts`; `apps/api/src/controllers/places.controller.ts` (9–103); `apps/api/src/controllers/rate-limit.controller.ts` -> Action: Add `JwtAuthGuard` (admin where appropriate); bind owners to JWT; encode `place_id`; disable redis-test, session demo, and rate-limit mutation in deployed environments.

CASCADE`.** `ensurePostsTable` (invoked from GET/POST post routes) can `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS posts CASCADE` when legacy columns are detected (78), plus likes/comments drops (309, 373–374). `tasks-schema.service.ts` (41) can drop `posts`. `DatabaseInit` drops donations/rides on startup (568, 670) when it decides the schema is legacy. - File: `apps/api/src/controllers/posts.controller.ts` (78, 309, 373–374); `apps/api/src/tasks/tasks-schema.service.ts` (41); `apps/api/src/database/database.init.ts` (568, 670) -> Action: Never DROP on a request path; gate destructive DDL behind an explicit offline migration.

## 🐞 Bugs & Logic Issues

 * **Unauthenticated posts feed treats query `user_id` as the viewer.** `GET /api/posts` has no guard. `feed_scope=friends` plus `user_id` filters to that user’s own posts and the people they follow (776–782) and the same id drives `is_liked`. Recommendation: Require JWT; bind viewer exclusively to `req.user.userId`; delete or auth-gate the likes/check and `viewer_id` query.

 * **Ride booking approval oversell.** `PUT /api/rides/bookings/:bookingId/status` (505–555) sets `approved` then only flips the ride to `full` after the fact — it does not reject when `approved + requested > available_seats`. Concurrent books can oversell. Recommendation: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` and reject when remaining seats are insufficient.

 * **Task hours-report catch returns success.** `GET /api/tasks/hours-report/:managerId` catch returns `success: true` with empty zeros, hiding failures. Recommendation: Return `success: false` and a generic error.

 * **Items-delivery / dedicated-items / collections static-route shadows.** `GET /api/items-delivery/:id` is declared before `GET requests`, so `GET /api/items-delivery/requests` hits `getItemById("requests")`. Dedicated-items `GET :id` shadows `GET search`. Collections `GET :collection` precedes `GET popular-collections` / `GET cache-stats` (those return 400 Invalid collection). Recommendation: Declare static routes before parameterized `:id` / `:collection`.

 * **`loginUser` / JWT guard never consult `user_profiles.is_active`.** Deactivated rows can still obtain a session via email-only login or an existing refresh token. Recommendation: Fail closed on `is_active = false` in login, resolve-id, refresh, and `JwtAuthGuard`.

 * **Anonymity filtering is specified but not implemented.** SRS §2.5.7 / NFR §3.2 require server-side redaction for `anonymity_level < 4`. The column is still absent from posts DDL (SRS §10; repo-wide search this run: 0 matches). Public feed returns author `id` / `name` / `avatar_url` for every post. Recommendation: Add the column + feed/by-id projection per SRS; do not treat this as a new product feature in a security hotfix PR.

 * **Personal-challenge reset-log `challengeId` is not ownership-checked.** `POST /api/challenges/reset-logs` overwrites `createDto.userId` from the JWT (507) then INSERTs any `challengeId` with no `challenges.user_id` match. Recommendation: INSERT only when `challenge_id` belongs to `CurrentUser()`.

 * **JwtAuthGuard non-access tokens fall through to Firebase JWKS (near-miss, not a bypass).** After `verifyToken` succeeds, `payload.type !== "access"` throws `UnauthorizedException` (123–125), which the inner `catch` treats as “try Firebase” (126–133). An HS256 refresh token fails Google JWKS, so this is not currently exploitable; it is a confused control-flow that can hide real JWT errors behind `Invalid Firebase token: …`. Recommendation: Re-throw `UnauthorizedException` from the type check; only fall back to Firebase when signature verification itself fails.

 * **Hand-rolled JWT signature compare is not constant-time.** `verifyTokenSignature` (`jwt.service.ts` 308) uses `!==` on the HMAC digest. Combined with the committed `JWT_SECRET` in `railway.toml.dev`, this is secondary to secret rotation. Recommendation: Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after length-checking; still rotate the committed secret.

 * **`getUserById` leaks `error.message` to clients.** Catch returns `{ success: false, error: "Failed to get user", details: error?.message }`. Production `ValidationPipe` `disableErrorMessages` does not cover this hand-rolled envelope. Recommendation: Return a generic error; log the details server-side only.

 * **Places `place_id` is interpolated unencoded.** `GET /place-details?place_id=` concatenates the query into the Google URL without `encodeURIComponent` (75). Autocomplete correctly encodes `input`. Recommendation: Encode `place_id`; consider allowlisting Place ID shape.

 * **ClosedRoute task-type / duplicate handling.** `apps/mobile/bottomBarScreens/profile/ClosedRoute.tsx` still uses an inline `require` of `databaseService`, `console.error`, and a loose `user?: any` prop. Recommendation: Use the shared logger; unify closed-content type tags; drop the inline `require`.

Stats admin-gates `analytics/users` but JWT-only-gates `details/:statType`. Rides has no guards at all. `SessionController` is registered in every environment despite DEMO/TEST file comments. `RedisTestController` is gated on `NODE_ENV !== "production"` rather than an explicit local-only flag, so the committed dev Railway template ships live Redis KEYS/GET/SET/DEL (2026-09-17).

 * **Positive in-folder contrasts (do not regress):** community-group-challenges binds creator from JWT on create/join/entry and uses `CurrentUser()` on `GET user/:userId/stats`, `GET :id/entries`, `PUT :id`, and `DELETE :id`; ChallengesController scopes personal timers to `CurrentUser()`; NotificationsController.`validateOwnership`; knowledge contribution-request binds `req.user.userId`; SyncController user/all/status use `AdminAuthGuard`; post DELETE binds session user without body fallback; authenticated chat send/read checks `ANY(participants)`; authenticated `GET conversations/user/:userId` already denies cross-user reads (do not delete that branch — apply it to guests too); `/session/login` correctly requires argon2 (contrast `/api/users/login`); CRM PATCH uses hardcoded column names (not `Object.keys`); mobile `WebViewScreen` does not take a caller-controlled URL.

 * **Operator matching workspace is specified, not implemented.** `OperatorAuthGuard` exists (`jwt-auth.guard.ts`) but there is no `/api/operator/*` module (zero operator controller files). Anonymity + matching-case audit tables remain SRS §10 gaps.

 * **196 source `.ts`/`.tsx` files exceed the ~200 LOC guideline.** Largest tracked source: `apps/mobile/utils/bubbles_Data.tsx` (4852). Mobile debt hubs: `databaseService.ts` (1225), `apiService.ts` (1055), duplicate `google_auth/SecureApiService.ts` (1165).
